mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impact.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) over a 3-month period signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input constraints and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand, which will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises > 5 points during the signal period, indicating the labor market weakness is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise significantly (> 10% YoY) and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a housing-driven demand boom that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: early-cycle recovery with easy monetary policy
failure_condition: Housing affordability index (NAR) falls below 100 during the signal period, indicating the housing boom is unsustainable.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over a 6-month period, exceeding 3%, signals an inflation scare that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in higher interest rates.
failure_condition: Breakeven inflation rates (10y TIPS) do not rise significantly (> 0.5pp) during the signal period, indicating the inflation scare is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 jobs per month for 3 consecutive months and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals a tight labor market that will boost wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows > 200k per month for 3 months and UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings (BLS) do not accelerate (> 0.2pp YoY) during the signal period, indicating the labor market tightness is not translating into wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: Real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) rising at an accelerating pace (> 5% YoY) signals strong consumer demand that will boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail inventories (Census Bureau) rise significantly (> 10% YoY) during the signal period, indicating the consumption boom is unsustainable and will lead to an inventory overhang.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with a rise in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) signals a stagflationary environment that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face input constraints and rising costs.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 2% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL rises > 2% in 6 months
failure_condition: The ISM manufacturing PMI rises above 50 during the signal period, indicating the industrial slowdown is temporary and not stagflationary.
